body.p: Half-faces. Once upon a time there was a man who had a mother, a wife and no father. It's just a story or a fairy tale. A kind of short story, or perhaps it was a fairy tale. This man hunts in this way by killing wild reindeer. The newly grown man turned out to be himself. A little boy lies in the cradle, he has him. Once a male reindeer was killed in the fall, during the onset of frost. Once the woman worked on the skin of the deer, the one with the bald antlers, its horns are already bald. Her husband is not at home, he is probably out hunting again. Grandmother came to her and said: "Sister- in-law, I'm telling you, I'd wear it like a deerskin with bare antlers, it would be good. Let me wear it. [She says:] Let me wear a deerskin with bare antlers! [She sings:] You and a man will live long. You will one day carry many more who were killed by you." [She says:] Her grandmother says. "How many animal skins he has killed, you will still wear. I won't live long. Let me wear this deerskin with bare antlers." The daughter-in-law barely makes it, she's all sweaty, the skin is thick. She said: "Oh, you're so-and-so! What a dog!" When she touched her with the scraper used to scrape the skin, the grandmother's neck broke off. When she stabbed her in the neck, her head rolled away. Her grandmother died, of course, because her head was cut off, she won't live [without her head]. Then she put her grandmother's head there, wrapped it around and wrapped her own grandmother a little. When the husband came in, [the woman] cried: "My grandmother is dead. The grandmother doesn't seem to be in the house, but outside. There was some kind of fur wrapped around them outside or something. The man simply said, "That morning when I left, because it was a good day, it was so bad because of the quick illness." As they sat there that evening, the grandmother's head came into the tent from under the floor of the door and said, "Son, I'll send you hunting from half of my bed, and I'll kiss my grandson from half of my bed." Here, she says, both are taken away. The daughter-in-law says: "And a word to me for the rest of my life." She said, "You, daughter-in-law, are the one who will go away, you are the one who will go away. When you take down the tent, you'll say one day and cry: "That poor tent we put up at Grandma's was ours, poor thing". You will recover. (They must have had many reindeer.) You'll be towing your wagon, and one day, when you're driving like this, the half-faces will be sitting at the end of your wagon saying, "Sister-in-law, we'll take care of your wagon, go ahead." From that moment on, you disappeared into the smoke, into the fog. I can't see you, you've gone somewhere," she says. "Now you're running away," she says to her son as she says for the second time, "I don't want you to stay here." Her son jumped into the street in the dark and grabbed the baby lying in the cradle, he must have been a big boy. And he's hiding somewhere. She lost him. He must have gone to the other side of the world, who knows where he went, she can't find her husband anywhere. The next morning, the woman (of course, how could it be otherwise, she won't be alone) hitched up her sledge and took down the tent. She wandered wherever she wanted. Where should she go? She cries a little and says: "Together with my grandmother, the tent used to be good." She was on the road, and one day, while she was driving like that, and it really was night, the half-faces were sitting on the sleigh, as it turned out. They say, "Daughter-in-law, we'll look after your sled, the noses of your sled won't get caught in the trees, drive even faster." She drove. She has disappeared somewhere, probably in the land of the dead, she will not go to the land of the living. This is the end.
